data.name: Jayalatha
data.gender_notes: Jayalatha is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Jaya: victory, Latha: prosperity. The name Jayalatha is derived from the Sanskrit language and represents the joy and success that comes with victory and prosperity. The name Jayalatha carries the meaning “Victory, Prosperity” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Jayalatha usually hope their child will grow to embody victory, prosperity and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Radiates strength and victory in all aspects of life.
data.etymology: Jayalatha belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Victory, Prosperity.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Jayalatha total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

data.cultural_impact: The name Jayalatha holds immense cultural significance in Hindu society, as it embodies the ideals of victory and prosperity. It is a name that instills confidence and carries a sense of pride. In Hindu mythology, the goddess Lakshmi, the deity of wealth and prosperity, is often invoked to bring immense wealth and victory in one's life. The name Jayalatha can be considered a reminder of the goddess' blessings.
data.spiritual_significance: Spiritually, the name Jayalatha symbolizes the victory of the soul over worldly desires and attachments. It signifies a person's triumph over material obstacles and worries, leading to inner peace and prosperity. The pursuit of material success should always be accompanied by spiritual growth, and the name Jayalatha serves as a constant reminder of this balance. As the name suggests, a person named Jayalatha is believed to be blessed with both worldly and spiritual prosperity.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Jayalatha: Victory (Jaya) over attachment (Latha). Embracing the spirit of triumph over earthly desires and material possessions.
